result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover all four moments well and rightly call the reminders browser notifications rather than email. A is tighter: it avoids timing promises and invented claims, and its shift-taken message says clearly that the parent wasn't signed up. B adds unsupported claims such as "It only takes a minute" and "you won't miss your shift", and suggests a reminder nudge on a screen that has no shifts. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover all four moments with short, friendly copy and correctly treat the reminders as browser notifications rather than email. B is more careful with claims: it avoids A's unsupported 'It only takes a minute' and implied timing ('before your shift', 'you won't miss your shift'), and its shift-taken message clearly states the parent was not signed up. A gives a slightly warmer reason for turning on reminders and a nice follow-up line after 'Not now', but that doesn't outweigh B's tighter discipline.
